title: Daily arXiv physics: 19 November 2026
global_caveat: This is an inferred ordering, not an official arXiv trending chart; citation evidence is limited for papers only about a day old.

sections.title: First observation of the Cabibbo-suppressed decay Bc+ to J/psi D*+
sections.abstract: LHCb reports a 5.4σ observation of the decay in 9 fb−1 of proton-proton data and measures its branching fraction relative to Bc+ to J/psi Ds+ as 0.067 ± 0.016 ± 0.003.
sections.ranking_evidence: First observation at 5.4 standard deviations, a measured branching-fraction ratio, and public machine-readable LHCb analysis material.
sections.claimed_result: The authors report the first observation and relative branching fraction, with statistical and systematic uncertainties, as a test of two-body Bc decay models.
sections.evidence_type: experimental; LHCb proton-proton collision data from 2011 to 2018 totaling 9 fb−1.
sections.unique_caveat: The statistical uncertainty (0.016) is substantially larger than the systematic uncertainty (0.003); simulation calibration of reconstruction and selection efficiencies is the leading systematic contribution.

sections.title: Observation of Exact Mobility-Edge Phases in Two-Dimensional Photonic Quasicrystals
sections.abstract: The authors derive exact mobility-edge conditions for a decorated two-dimensional Aubry–André quasicrystal and probe extended, localized, and partially localized regimes in photonic waveguide lattices using quench dynamics.
sections.ranking_evidence: An analytical mobility-edge prediction is paired with a fabricated photonic-lattice demonstration of energy-dependent localization and a resonant flat-band state.
sections.claimed_result: The authors report a route to exact two-dimensional mobility edges and an experimental photonic realization, described as, to their knowledge, the first observation of mobility-edge phases in two dimensions.
sections.evidence_type: theoretical and experimental; exact lattice analysis, femtosecond-laser-written photonic waveguides, and quench-propagation measurements.
sections.unique_caveat: The experiment is a controlled photonic analogue in a finite engineered lattice, not electronic localization in a material; transfer to other platforms and higher dimensions remains to be tested.

sections.title: The role of externally-driven density fluctuations in the enhancement of beam spray
sections.abstract: Experiments show that speckled 351-nm heater beams increase the spray of a separate 1053-nm beam after plasma propagation; modeling attributes the enhancement to long-wavelength plasma-density fluctuations.
sections.ranking_evidence: A measured beam-propagation change is paired with physical modeling and propagation simulations; the arXiv comment reports submission to Physical Review Letters.
sections.claimed_result: In the OMEGA experiment, the 95%-energy angular spray measure increased from 12.7 mrad in the vacuum reference to 33.8 mrad with heater beams on; modeling and simulations connect the effect to heater-driven plasma fluctuations.
sections.evidence_type: experimental and computational; OMEGA heater and probe beams, gas-jet plasma, Thomson-scattering diagnostics, fluctuation modeling, and beam-propagation simulations.
sections.unique_caveat: The measurement is specific to the reported laser/plasma geometry; large density-fluctuation amplitudes are model estimates, not an independent direct measurement of the full fluctuation spectrum.

sections.title: LEMUR: A Searchable Web Archive of Deep Chandra Images of Galaxies and Galaxy Clusters
sections.abstract: LEMUR releases uniformly reduced Chandra images for 2,569 galaxies and clusters, using 5,505 ACIS observations and 138.8 Ms of exposure, with a searchable archive, catalog, and open code.
sections.ranking_evidence: A large reusable X-ray release is paired with Zenodo tables and open-source processing code; the authors report a 3% broad-band photometry agreement against the Chandra Source Catalog for 275 point sources.
sections.claimed_result: The archive provides merged Chandra products and a morphology search; AstroCLIP-nearest cluster pairs share cool-core status in 73% of matches versus 51% by chance.
sections.evidence_type: computational and data release; archival Chandra ACIS observations reprocessed with CIAO, plus a searchable web archive, Zenodo tables, and GitHub code.
sections.unique_caveat: The authors note incomplete coverage, possible target-grouping errors, residual background, and an approximately 20% soft-band flux underestimate from a single-energy exposure-map approximation; similarity is morphological, not a calibrated physical distance.

sections.title: Fluctuations and Correlations of Conserved Charges in Isobar Collisions at sqrt(sNN)=200 GeV with the STAR Detector
sections.abstract: STAR measures second-order cumulants and correlations of conserved-charge proxies in Ru+Ru and Zr+Zr collisions; the results are compared with lattice-QCD and UrQMD calculations.
sections.ranking_evidence: Collider measurements are directly compared with lattice-QCD and transport calculations; a DOI and a related STAR conference presentation are available.
sections.claimed_result: Peripheral-collision ratios follow the ordering predicted by lattice QCD for matter in an external magnetic field; UrQMD gives a similar hierarchy but underpredicts the peripheral-to-central enhancement.
sections.evidence_type: experimental; STAR Ru+Ru and Zr+Zr collisions at sqrt(sNN)=200 GeV, compared with lattice-QCD and UrQMD calculations.
sections.unique_caveat: Agreement with the magnetic-field-motivated lattice ordering does not isolate magnetic-field effects from other sources of centrality dependence; the authors call for further quantitative study.

sections.title: Producing μBq/m3-level low-226Ra ultrapure water for the Jiangmen Underground Neutrino Observatory
sections.abstract: JUNO reports a sensitive radium assay and a 100-ton-per-hour water process producing water below 4 μBq/m3 of 226Ra, under the detector's 50 μBq/m3 requirement.
sections.ranking_evidence: An engineering-scale detector-enabling result reports a quantified assay threshold and production rate; the paper has a journal reference and DOI.
sections.claimed_result: Selective ion-exchange resin and membrane separation produced water consistently below 4 μBq/m3 of radium, compared with JUNO's specified limit of 50 μBq/m3.
sections.evidence_type: experimental; high-sensitivity radium measurements and operation/validation of the JUNO ultrapure-water purification train at 100 t/h.
sections.unique_caveat: Performance is demonstrated for JUNO's specified process and engineering scale; assay sensitivity and site-specific water conditions bound how broadly it transfers.

sections.title: Map-Level Inference of Primordial Gravitational Waves from the CMB with Spherical Neural Networks
sections.abstract: A spherical graph-convolution network estimates r directly from simulated multifrequency CMB B-mode maps, improving RMSE by 1.3 times and narrowing 68% intervals by 1.2 times versus a matched likelihood in the tested setup.
sections.ranking_evidence: Benchmarked against a likelihood on 20,000 simulations with quantified changes in point error and interval width; cross-listed in cosmology and instrumentation.
sections.claimed_result: The authors find improved simulated r recovery without explicit power-spectrum estimation or component separation; saliency maps favor deeper sky regions and cleaner frequency channels.
sections.evidence_type: computational; spherical graph convolution tested on 20,000 simulated multifrequency CMB maps with lensing, noise, dust, and synchrotron foregrounds.
sections.unique_caveat: Both methods inherit foreground assumptions; the authors report failed generalization to a three-dimensional dust model with line-of-sight variation. This is a simulation result, not a detection.

sections.title: Rapid Equation of State Inference from Multiprobe Datasets
sections.abstract: A joint analysis of binary-neutron-star gravitational waves, NICER mass-radius data, and massive-pulsar timing infers R1.4=11.93 (+1.02/−0.83) km and Mmax=2.31±0.23 solar masses at 90% credible level.
sections.ranking_evidence: Combines three observational channels that probe distinct density regimes and reports numerical posterior constraints; cross-listing connects neutron-star astrophysics and gravitational physics.
sections.claimed_result: The authors find that gravitational-wave and NICER data constrain low-to-intermediate densities while massive pulsars constrain high densities; they report no simple mapping between EoS stiffness and Bayesian evidence.
sections.evidence_type: observational and computational; Bayesian inference using binary-neutron-star gravitational waves, NICER X-ray mass-radius data, and radio timing of massive pulsars.
sections.unique_caveat: Constraints depend on the parameterized equation of state and candidate-model choices; current multimessenger data do not identify a unique microscopic composition.

sections.title: Simultaneous spectral measurement and programmable filtering on a universal silicon photonic chip
sections.abstract: A fabricated silicon photonic chip combines programmable spectral filtering and measurement, demonstrating 0.05-nm resolution over more than 100 nm of bandwidth while measuring eight laser sources.
sections.ranking_evidence: A hardware demonstration quantifies bandwidth and resolution and shows filter reconfiguration during measurement.
sections.claimed_result: The authors report simultaneous measurement and programmable filtering on one universal linear-optical circuit with dynamic filter reconfiguration.
sections.evidence_type: experimental; fabricated silicon photonic chip with two 8×8 programmable unitary circuits, intensity modulators, and eight laser inputs.
sections.unique_caveat: The reported performance is from one fabricated prototype; repeatability and long-term stability are not quantified in the abstract checked.
